question: The battle of Khanwa was fought between the forces of the Babur and the Rajput forces led by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Sanga**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Khanwa was fought in 1527 between the Mughal Emperor Babur and the Rajput forces led by Rana Sanga of Mewar.**
 
• It** was a significant battle that marked the consolidation of Mughal power in India.**
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, led the Mughal forces, while Rana Sanga, the ruler of Mewar, led the Rajput confederacy.
 
• **The battle was triggered by Babur's desire to expand his empire **and control the fertile plains of North India.
 
• Rana Sanga,** as the leading Rajput ruler, opposed Babur's ambitions and formed a confederacy of Rajput states to resist Mughal expansion.**
 
• The **battle took place on March 17, 1527,** near the town of Khanwa in Rajasthan.
 
• Babur employed innovative military tactics, including the use of artillery and the "chakar-i-barbar" (the "whirlwind" formation), to defeat the Rajput forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ibrahim Lodi:
 
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, which ruled Delhi and parts of North India before the arrival of the Mughals.
 
• Ibrahim Lodi clashed with Babur over territorial disputes, leading to the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, where Babur defeated Lodi and established Mughal rule in North India.
 
 
 
• Medini Rai:
 
 
• Medini Rai was a Rajput ruler of Chanderi, a state in central India.
 
• He joined Rana Sanga's confederacy against Babur but was defeated and killed in the Battle of Khanwa
 
 
 
• Mahmud Lodi
 
 
• Mahmud Lodi was the second ruler of the Lodi dynasty, which ruled Delhi and parts of North India from 1451 to 1526.
 
• He succeeded his father, Bahlol Lodi, and reigned from 1489 to 1517.
